column5: Look: tactile tabletop diorama *(provisional)*. Mood: a war game on a table, warm and toy-like. Little stone keeps on a parchment-and-green-felt map; each level adds a visible storey and a bigger banner. Troops are tiny pawn figures marching single file along a rope-like link. Palette: player royal blue, rival crimson, neutral grey stone, ground parchment and felt, accent gold for level-ups; shadows cool, lights warm. Detail on keeps and banners; the map behind is quiet. Signature: links drawn as taut ropes pinned between keeps that sag when cut. Every figure drawn, no emoji, no plain circles.
References: Galcon, Mushroom Wars (the send-and-conquer loop); Tentacle Wars (persistent links).
View: 2D · Camera: fixed top-down, portrait phone layout, the whole map in view.
Drag to link two keeps; swipe to cut a link
Troops generate periodically; keeps level 1→3 by troop count; level sets max links (1/2/3) and generation speed
Pawns march along links; hitting an enemy keep reduces its garrison and takes it at zero; hitting your own reinforces
Opposing marches on the same link fight where they meet *(guessed)*
Neutral keeps hold a garrison and don't generate *(guessed)*
One AI rival that expands, attacks weak keeps and defends *(provisional)*
5 maps with a map-select ladder, win/lose screens, restart
Juice: banner pop on capture, level-up flourish, rope snap and sag, marching sounds

You start with one blue level-1 keep, its troop count ticking up; grey neutral keeps sit nearby with small garrisons.
A pulsing hint shows a drag to the nearest neutral; you drag, a rope snaps between them, and pawns march.
The garrison counts down, hits zero, and flips blue with a banner pop.
Your first keep passes the threshold and grows to level 2 — it can now hold a second rope; you link another neutral.
The red rival, far off, is doing the same: the race for the middle is on.
Map 1 is a gentle race for neutrals.
From map 2 the rival attacks your thinnest keep, and you must cut and reroute ropes to defend.
A loss restarts that map.
Later maps add more keeps, a stronger rival start and a faster rival *(provisional)*.
